paragraphs: Safe Bulkers, Inc. was incorporated in the Republic of the Marshall Islands on December 11, 2007, for the purpose of acquiring ownership of various subsidiaries that either owned or were scheduled to own vessels. Polys Hajioannou, our chief executive officer, has a long history of operating and investing in the international shipping industry, including a long history of vessel ownership. Vassos Hajioannou, the late father of Polys Hajioannou, our chief executive officer, first invested in shipping in 1958. Polys Hajioannou has been actively involved in the industry since 1987, when he joined the predecessor of Safety Management.

Over the past 39 years under the leadership of Polys Hajioannou, we have sold or contracted to sell 31 drybulk vessels during periods of what we viewed as favorable second-hand market conditions and have contracted to acquire 72 drybulk newbuilds and 13 drybulk second-hand vessels. Also under his leadership, we have expanded the classes of drybulk vessels in our fleet and the aggregate carrying capacity of our fleet has grown from 887,900 dwt prior to our initial public offering in May 28, 2008 to 4,559,000 dwt as of February 20, 2026. Information on our capital expenditure requirements are discussed in "Item 5. Operating and Financial Review and Prospects—B. Liquidity and Capital Resources." More recently after 2020, we have initiated an extensive fleet renewal and upgrade program by which we have ordered 20 newbuilds with advance energy efficiency characteristics with deliveries from 2022 onwards, on top of 11 existing ships built after 2014 with superior energy efficiency characteristics compared to pre-2014 designs, known as eco-ships; environmentally upgraded 26 existing vessels and sold, or contracted to sell, 17 older vessels, replaced with seven younger second-hand vessels in order to establish a competitive advantage in the developing environment towards decarbonization. The quality and size of our current fleet, together with our long-term relationships with several of our charter customers, are, we believe, the results of our long-term strategy of maintaining a high quality fleet, our broad knowledge of the drybulk industry and our strong management team. In addition to

benefiting from the experience and leadership of Polys Hajioannou, we also benefit from the expertise of our Managers which, along with their predecessor, have specialized in drybulk shipping since 1965. In June 2008, we completed an initial public offering of our Common Stock in the U.S. and our Common Stock began trading on the NYSE. Our principal executive office is located at Apt. D11, Les Acanthes, 6, Avenue des Citronniers MC 98000 Monaco. Our registered address in the Republic of the Marshall Islands is Trust Company Complex, Ajeltake Road, Ajeltake Island, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands, MH96960 and telephone numbers are +30 2 111 888 400 and +357 25 887 200. The name of our registered agent at such address is The Trust Company of the Marshall Islands, Inc.
The SEC maintains an internet site at http://www.sec.gov that contains reports, information statements, and other information regarding issuers that we file electronically with the SEC.

We are an international provider of marine drybulk transportation services, that owns and operates a modern and diverse fleet of dry bulk vessels, transporting bulk cargoes, particularly coal, grain and iron ore, along worldwide shipping routes for some of the world's largest consumers of marine drybulk transportation services. As of February 20, 2026, we had a fleet of 45 drybulk vessels, with an aggregate carrying capacity of 4,559,000 dwt.

We employ our vessels on both period time charters and spot time charters, according to our assessment of market conditions, with some of the world's largest consumers of marine drybulk transportation services. The vessels we deploy on period time charters provide us with relatively stable cash flow and high utilization rates, while the vessels we deploy in the spot market allow us to maintain our flexibility in low charter market conditions. We are focused on owning a modern, well-maintained fleet with the best designs in the shipping dry-bulk sector, targeting to reduce the environmental impact from our operations. Over the past several years, we have made publicly available our annual sustainability report, where we present in detail our environmental, social and governance strategy for the future, as well as the impact of our operations and business on society and the environment. We believe that integrating ESG at the very heart of our corporate strategy, will enable us to continue to have access to capital, enjoy existing and future investors' trust, reduce our fleets' carbon footprint and remain competitive in the dry bulk market.

During previous years, a number of countries and the IMO, have adopted regulatory frameworks to reduce GHG emissions (increased energy efficiency standards for existing vessels and newbuilds, classification of vessels on the basis of annual CO2 emissions, cap and trade regimes, carbon taxes and penalties, and incentives or mandates for using alternative fuels with lower carbon footprint compared to fossil fuels or using renewable energy), due to concerns over the risk of climate change. GHG emissions reduction measures may impose operational and financial restrictions affecting increasingly more the less efficient vessels, reducing their trade and competitiveness, increasing their environmental compliance costs, imposing additional energy efficiency investments, or even making such older, less energy efficient vessels obsolete. The environmental initiatives are complemented with initiatives towards the local societies where we operate and the way our company is governed, altogether included in a framework known as Environmental, Social and Governance or "ESG". Investor advocacy groups, certain institutional investors, investment funds, lenders and other market participants are increasingly focused on ESG practices hindering access to capital and reallocating capital as a result of their assessment of a company's ESG practices.

Safe Bulkers, targeting to reduce the environmental impact of our operations, and increase the sustainability of our business over time, has placed and integrated ESG at the heart of our corporate strategy and has undertaken significant investments with the purpose of increasing our fleet's environmental competitiveness and successfully meet society's expectations as to our proper role. In light of investors' increased focus on ESG matters and in response to the GHG environmental regulations, we have assessed the applicability of relevant energy efficiency measures, and decided to pursue a two-fold strategy: i) a comprehensive fleet renewal program consisting of several newbuild orders with advanced energy efficiency characteristics, the acquisition of younger second-hand vessels and the sale of older, less efficient vessels at suitable times and ii) an extensive program for environmental upgrading of existing vessels in our fleet during their dry-dockings.

As of February 20, 2026, our fleet consisted of 45 vessels, one of which was held for sale, 11 of which are eco-ships built after 2014, with superior energy efficiency characteristics compared to pre-2014 designs, and 12 vessels built 2022 onwards, compliant with the most recent IMO GHG Phase 3 - NOx Tier III regulations. In addition, the Company's outstanding orderbook consists of eight newbuilds compliant with the IMO GHG Phase 3 - NOx Tier III regulations, including two methanol dual fueled, to be delivered four in 2026, two in 2027, one in 2028 and one in 2029 and following all scheduled deliveries, reaching 31 vessels with improved energy efficiency characteristics. The aggregate capital expenditure for the 20 newbuilds was approximately $734.9 million.

During the last five years and until February 20, 2026, the Company has sold or contracted to sell 17 vessels with total deadweight of 1.5 million tonnes and of 15.0 years average age with aggregate gross sale proceeds of $297.1 million and acquired seven second-hand vessels with total deadweight of 1.0 million tonnes and of 9.2 years average age at an aggregate gross acquisition cost of $187.0 million.

In parallel and as of February 20, 2026, we have completed environmental upgrades on 26 vessels through an extensive vessel environmental upgrade program which involves application of low friction paints and installation of energy saving device.While we are investing in newbuilds, relatively young second-hand vessels and environmental upgrades, we continue to monitor technological developments in relation to new environmentally friendly alternative marine fuels, which we expect will play an increasingly important role in the next decade.

As of February 20, 2026, we have installed Scrubbers on 21 of our vessels, including in all eight of our Capesize class vessels, effectively reducing SOx emissions compared to VLSFO and capitalizing on our Scrubber investments in relation to price differential between VLSFO and HSFO. The total cost of the Scrubber investments has amounted to $57.7 million, which we estimate we have already recovered through the additional earnings of the Scrubber-fitted vessels. As of February 20, 2026, we have retrofitted our entire fleet with BWTS.

On the financing front, during 2025, aligning financing with our corporate sustainability agenda we secured a new sustainability-linked financing of $75 million for six vessels incorporating a mechanism that adjusts the interest margin based on independently verified performance related to fleet carbon intensity index, measured against annual sustainability performance targets, and amended the terms of an existing $100 million financing for six vessels to include similar terms.

In 2023, we established our environmental, social and governance board committee. The ESG Committee which consists of six board members, four of whom are independent directors, reviews the Company's ESG performance and ensures governance oversight by the Board of Directors of the ESG strategy and implementation, consistent with the priorities outlined and articulated in the Company's annual sustainability report.

This discussion includes forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. As a result of many factors, such as those set forth under "Item 3. Key Information—D. Risk Factors" and elsewhere in this annual report, our actual results may differ materially from those anticipated in these forward-looking statements. Please see the section "Forward-Looking Statements" at the beginning of this annual report.

Our business is to provide international marine drybulk transportation services by operating vessels in the drybulk sector of the shipping industry. We deploy our vessels on a mix of period time and spot time charters according to our assessment of market conditions, adjusting the mix of these charters to take advantage of the relatively stable cash flow and high utilization rates associated with period time charters, or to profit from attractive spot time charter rates during periods of strong charter market conditions, or to maintain employment flexibility that the spot market offers during periods of weak time charter market conditions. We believe our customers, some of which have been chartering our vessels for over 27 years, enter into period time and spot time charters with us because of the quality of our modern vessels and our record of safe and efficient operations.

Our operations are managed by our Managers, Safety Management, Safe Bulkers Management Ltd., and Safe Bulkers Management Monaco, under the supervision of our executive officers and our board of directors. Under our Management Agreements, our Managers provide us with technical, administrative and commercial services and our executive management. All three of our Managers are controlled by Polys Hajioannou. See "Item 7. Major Shareholders and Related Party Transactions—B. Related Party Transactions—Management Agreements" for more information.

paragraphs: Safe Bulkers, Inc. 於馬紹爾羣島共和國於 2007 年 12 月 11 日成立，目的是取得各種子公司的所有權，這些子公司或是擁有或是預計會擁有船舶。Polys Hajioannou，我們的首席執行官，有長期經營與投資國際航運產業的經驗，包括長期擁有船舶的經驗。Vassos Hajioannou，Polys Hajioannou，我們的首席執行官的已故父親，於 1958 年首次投資航運產業。Polys Hajioannou 自 1987 年起積極參與此產業，當時他加入 Safety Management 的前身。

在 Polys Hajioannou 領導下過去 39 年，我們已出售或訂約出售 31 艘乾散貨船，是在我們認為有利的二手船市場條件期間，並已訂約取得 72 艘乾散貨新造船與 13 艘乾散貨二手船。在他的領導下，我們也擴展了我們船隊中乾散貨船的船型，並於我們 2008 年 5 月 28 日首次公開發行前，船隊總載重噸數為 887,900 dwt，至 2026 年 2 月 20 日已成長為 4,559,000 dwt。關於我們的資本支出需求，請參閱「第 5 項。營運與財務審閱與展望—B. 流動性與資本資源」。更近來在 2020 年後，我們已啟動一項廣泛的船隊更新與升級計畫，我們已訂購 20 艘具先進能源效率特性的新造船，預計於 2022 年後交付，加上 11 艘於 2014 年後建造、相比預 2014 年設計更優秀能源效率的現有船舶，稱為 eco-ships；並已對 26 艘現有船舶進行環境升級，並出售或訂約出售 17 艘較舊船舶，以七艘較年輕的二手船取代，以建立在朝向減碳環境中競爭優勢。我們目前船隊的品質與規模，加上我們與部分租賃客戶的長期關係，我們認為是我們長期策略維持高品質船隊、對乾散貨產業廣泛知識與強大管理團隊的結果。此外

除了受益於 Polys Hajioannou 的經驗與領導，我們也受益於我們經理人的專業知識，他們及其前身自 1965 年以來專門從事乾散貨航運。我們於 2008 年 6 月完成美國的首次公開發行，發行普通股，並於紐約證券交易所開始交易。我們的總部位於 Monaco 的 Les Acanthes, 6, Avenue des Citronniers MC 98000。我們在馬紹爾羣島共和國的註冊地址為 Trust Company Complex, Ajeltake Road, Ajeltake Island, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands, MH96960，電話為 +30 2 111 888 400 和 +357 25 887 200。我們在該地址的註冊代理人為 The Trust Company of the Marshall Islands, Inc。
SEC 保有網際網路網站於 http://www.sec.gov，包含我們向 SEC 提交的電子檔報告、資訊聲明及其他資訊。
我們是國際提供海洋乾散貨運輸服務的供應商，擁有並營運現代且多樣化的乾散貨船隊，運輸大宗貨物，特別是煤炭、穀物與鐵礦，沿全球航運路線為世界最大規模的海洋乾散貨運輸服務消費者服務。截至 2026 年 2 月 20 日，我們擁有 45 艘乾散貨船，總載重噸數為 4,559,000 dwt。

我們根據市場條件，將船舶出租於定期租賃與即時租賃，與一些世界最大規模的海洋乾散貨運輸服務消費者合作。我們出租於定期租賃的船舶，為我們帶來相對穩定的現金流與高使用率，而我們出租於即時市場的船舶則讓我們在低租賃市場條件下保持靈活性。我們專注於擁有現代、維護良好的船隊，並擁有乾散貨航運領域最佳的設計，目標是減少我們運營的環境影響。在過去幾年，我們已公開我們的年度可持續性報告，詳細說明我們未來的環境、社會與治理策略，以及我們運營與業務對社會與環境的影響。我們認為將 ESG 整合至我們企業策略的核心，將使我們持續獲得資金，享有現有與未來投資者的信任，減少船隊的碳足跡，並在乾散貨市場中保持競爭力。

在過去幾年，許多國家與國際海事組織（IMO）已採納規範架構以減少 GHG 排放（提高現有船舶與新造船的能源效率標準、根據年度二氧化碳排放量對船舶進行分類、碳交易制度、碳稅與處罰，以及使用較低碳足跡替代燃料或可再生能源的激勵措施或強制規定），由於對氣候變遷風險的擔憂。減少 GHG 排放的措施可能對運營與財務造成限制，影響越來越不具效率的船舶，減少其貿易與競爭力，增加其環境合規成本，要求進行額外的能源效率投資，甚至使這些較舊、較不具能源效率的船舶過時。環境倡議措施與我們運營地的當地社會及公司治理方式相輔相成，整體納入一個稱為環境、社會與治理（ESG）的架構。投資者倡議團體、某些機構投資者、投資基金、貸款人及其他市場參與者日益關注 ESG 緣由，這可能影響資金取得並導致資金重新配置，基於他們對公司 ESG 緣由的評估。

Safe Bulkers，目標是減少我們運營的環境影響，並逐步提高我們業務的可持續性，已將 ESG 整合至我們企業策略的核心，並已進行重大投資，目的是提高我們船隊的環境競爭力，並成功符合社會對我們適當角色的期望。根據投資者對 ESG 事項的關注度，並回應 GHG 環境規範，我們已評估相關能源效率措施的適用性，並決定採用雙重策略：i) 一項全面的船隊更新計畫，包括多個具先進能源效率特性的新造船訂單、購入較年輕的二手船與在合適時機出售較舊、較不具效率的船舶；ii) 一項針對我們船隊現有船舶在船廠停泊期間進行環境升級的廣泛計畫。

截至2026年2月20日，本公司船隊總計有45艘船舶，其中1艘為待售，11艘為2014年後建造的生態船，其能源效率優於2014年前的設計，且12艘為2022年起建造的船舶，符合最新IMO GHG Phase 3 - NOx Tier III規範。此外，本公司現有訂單簿包含8艘新造船，符合IMO GHG Phase 3 - NOx Tier III規範，其中包括2艘甲醇雙燃料船，預計於2026年交付4艘，2027年交付2艘，2028年交付1艘，2029年交付1艘，於所有預計交付後，總計達31艘具備改善能源效率特性的船舶。20艘新造船的總資本支出約為734.9 百萬美元。
於最近五年及至2026年2月20日，本公司已出售或訂立出售合約共17艘船舶，總載重為1.5百萬公噸，平均船齡為15.0年，累計毛銷售收入為297.1百萬美元，並取得七艘二手船舶，總載重為1.0百萬公噸，平均船齡為9.2年，累計毛取得成本為187.0百萬美元。
同時，截至2026年2月20日，本公司已完成26艘船舶的環境升級，透過廣泛的船舶環境升級計畫，包括應用低摩擦塗料及安裝節能裝置。雖然本公司正在投資新造船、相對年輕的二手船舶及環境升級，但我們持續監測與新環保替代船用燃料相關的技術發展，預期這些技術在未來十年將扮演越來越重要的角色。
截至2026年2月20日，本公司已在21艘船舶上安裝脫硫裝置，包括所有8艘Capesize級船舶，有效降低SOx排放，相比VLSFO，並利用脫硫裝置投資，以VLSFO與HSFO的價格差異獲利。脫硫裝置投資總成本為57.7 百萬美元，我們估計已透過裝設脫硫裝置的船舶額外營收回收該成本。截至2026年2月20日，本公司已將整體船隊進行BWTS retrofit。
在資金籌措方面，2025年，配合本公司企業永續議程，我們取得一筆新永續連結融資，金額為75 百萬美元，用於6艘船舶，包含根據獨立驗證的船隊碳強度指數表現，調整利率邊際的機制，並修改一筆現有100 百萬美元融資的條款，用於6艘船舶，包含類似條款。
2023年，本公司設立環境、社會及治理（ESG）委員會。該ESG委員會由6位董事組成，其中4位為獨立董事，審查本公司ESG表現，並確保董事會對ESG策略及執行的治理監督，符合本公司年度永續報告中所說明的優先事項與表達重點。

paragraphs: 下列關於本公司財務狀況與營運成果之討論，應配合本年度財務報表及其附註說明一併閱讀。此討論包含前瞻性聲明，涉及風險與不確定性。由於許多因素，例如於「項目 3. 重要資訊—D. 風險因素」及本年度報告其他部分所列述者，本公司實際結果可能與此前瞻性聲明所預期者有重大差異。請參閱本年度報告開頭之「前瞻性聲明」部分。

本公司業務為提供國際散裝貨運運輸服務，透過經營散裝貨運業之船舶。本公司根據市場狀況評估，將船舶部署於不同之期租與現租合約，調整此兩種合約之組合，以利用期租合約所帶來相對穩定之現金流與高使用率，或於租賃市場條件良好時，獲取具吸引力之現租合約租金，或於租賃市場條件不佳時，維持現租市場所提供的就業靈活性。本公司相信，部分客戶（其中一些客戶已租賃本公司船舶逾 27 年）與本公司簽訂期租與現租合約，係因本公司現代化船舶之品質與安全且高效之營運紀錄。

本公司營運由本公司經理、安全管理、Safe Bulkers Management Ltd. 及 Safe Bulkers Management Monaco 管理，並在本公司高階管理人員與董事會監督之下進行。根據本公司管理協議，本公司經理為本公司提供技術、行政與商業服務及本公司高階管理。本公司所有經理皆由 Polys Hajioannou 控制。有關更多資訊，請參閱「項目 7. 主要股東與關聯交易—B. 關聯交易—管理協議」。
下表呈現 Safe Bulkers, Inc. 於最近五年內截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止各年度之選取合併財務及其他資料。Safe Bulkers, Inc. 之選取合併財務資料為總結、衍生自並受本公司經會計師核閱之合併財務報表及其附註說明之限制，該等財務報表已依美國（「美國」）一般會計準則（「美國 GAAP」）編製。
本公司經會計師核閱之合併損益表、股東權益變動表及現金流量表，係截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日、2024 年 12 月 31 日及 2025 年 12 月 31 日之年度資料，以及截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日及 2025 年 12 月 31 日之合併資產負債表，連同其附註說明，請參閱「項目 18. 財務報表」，並應完整閱讀。
